definition: The state or experience of finding something funny, or the provision of entertainment
examples: She looked at the playful puppy with great amusement.

definition: A strong feeling of annoyance, displeasure, or hostility
examples: He found it difficult to control his anger after hearing the unfair decision.

definition: A feeling of worry, nervousness, or unease about something with an uncertain outcome
examples: Waiting for exam results often causes a lot of anxiety among students.

definition: In any way; to any extent; or used as a polite reply to thank you
examples: I am not at all surprised by the outcome of the match.

definition: Responsible for an undesirable situation or mistake; in the wrong
examples: The investigation showed that the other driver was clearly at fault.

definition: In the end; after a long delay, dispute, or series of problems
examples: After hours of waiting in the rain, the bus arrived at last.

definition: Immediately; or at the same time
examples: When the alarm rang, everyone left the building at once.

definition: At risk to be won or lost; in danger
examples: With the championship title at stake, both teams played their hardest.

definition: Unintentionally; without planning to do so
examples: I deleted the important file from my computer completely by accident.

definition: Accidental; in error
examples: Someone took my umbrella from the restaurant stand by mistake.

definition: To take action to reduce, destroy, or prevent something undesirable
examples: The government introduced new measures to combat rising crime rates.

definition: To perpetrate or carry out a mistake, crime, or immoral act
examples: The suspect proved that he could not have been the one to commit the crime.

definition: The action or power of focusing one's attention or mental effort
examples: Loud noises in the street broke his concentration while he was studying.

definition: A state of happiness and satisfaction
examples: He sighed with contentment as he sat by the warm fireplace.

definition: The use of the imagination or original ideas, especially in the production of an artistic work
examples: Art and music classes encourage children to express their creativity.

definition: To make an opening, incision, or wound in something with a sharp-edged tool or object
examples: Be careful with that sharp knife so you don't cut your finger.

definition: The action or process of making important decisions
examples: Clear thinking and logic are essential for effective decision making.

definition: To discourage someone from doing something by instilling doubt or fear of the consequences
examples: Security cameras were installed to deter thieves from entering the building.

definition: A natural instinctive state of mind deriving from one's circumstances, mood, or relationships with others
examples: Her voice trembled with emotion as she thanked her family for their support.

definition: A feeling of discontented or resentful longing aroused by someone else's possessions, qualities, or luck
examples: He looked at his neighbor's brand-new sports car with a touch of envy.

definition: Permanently; forever
examples: After living abroad for ten years, she decided to return home for good.

definition: Until a later time; for the present
examples: We can leave the boxes in the hallway for now and unpack them tomorrow.

definition: Used to introduce the first of two or more reasons or considerations
examples: I don't want to buy that coat; for one thing, it is far too expensive.

definition: For the present; until some other arrangement is made
examples: You can use my spare laptop for the time being until yours is repaired.

definition: The feeling of being upset or annoyed, especially because of inability to change or achieve something
examples: He shouted in frustration when his computer crashed before he saved his work.

definition: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills
examples: Solving complex puzzles requires patience and high intelligence.

definition: The method of human communication, either spoken or written, consisting of the use of words in a structured way
examples: Learning a foreign language opens up many new career opportunities.

definition: Reasoning conducted or assessed according to strict principles of validity
examples: If you apply basic logic to the problem, the solution becomes obvious.

definition: The faculty by which the mind stores and remembers information
examples: She has an excellent memory for names, faces, and historical dates.

definition: A state or feeling of great distress or discomfort of mind or body
examples: The cold rain and freezing wind added to the misery of the lost hikers.

definition: Interesting; worth knowing or noticing
examples: This new documentary will be of interest to anyone studying marine biology.

word: on the one hand ... on the other hand
definition: Used to present two contrasting factors or points of view
examples: On the one hand I'd like a job that pays more, but on the other hand I enjoy the free time I have now.
translation: с одно́й стороны́ ... с друго́й стороны́

definition: Having reconsidered a matter and reached a different decision
examples: I was going to order the steak, but on second thoughts, I'll have the fish.

definition: Taking everything into account; in general
examples: There were a few minor delays, but on the whole the conference went very well.

definition: The ability to see, hear, or become aware of something through the senses, or a way of understanding something
examples: Optical illusions trick the brain and alter our visual perception.

definition: Of little importance; trivial
examples: They wasted the entire meeting arguing over petty details.

definition: The action of stopping something from happening or arising
examples: In medicine, disease prevention is always better than cure.

definition: The process of making plans for something
examples: Careful financial planning is necessary before starting a new business.

definition: The process of finding solutions to difficult or complex issues
examples: Programming teaches students logical thinking and creative problem solving.

definition: A measure, quantity, or frequency, typically one measured against some other quantity or measure
examples: The city's unemployment rate has dropped significantly this year.

definition: To set down in writing or some other permanent form for later reference, or to capture sound or images
examples: Scientists record the temperature of the water twice a day.

definition: Conscious knowledge of one's own character, feelings, motives, and desires
examples: Developing self-awareness helps you understand your strengths and weaknesses.

definition: A physical feeling or perception resulting from something that happens to or comes into contact with the body
examples: He felt a tingling sensation in his fingers after coming in from the cold.

definition: A painful feeling of humiliation or distress caused by the consciousness of wrong or foolish behavior
examples: He hung his head in shame after being caught cheating on the test.

definition: The expression of or the ability to express thoughts and feelings by articulate sounds
examples: The left hemisphere of the brain is largely responsible for human speech.

definition: A state of mental or emotional strain or tension resulting from adverse or very demanding circumstances
examples: Regular exercise and meditation are effective ways to reduce daily stress.

definition: A sudden feeling of excitement and pleasure
examples: Winning the competition gave the young athlete an unforgettable thrill.

definition: In the custody of the police
examples: The police officer informed the suspect that he was under arrest.

definition: Being dealt with or managed successfully; not out of hand
examples: Firefighters worked through the night and finally got the forest fire under control.

definition: Believing, usually mistakenly, that something is the case
examples: I was under the impression that the meeting started at ten o'clock, not nine.
